title: Client Transport Transition Playbook and Migration Requirements
creator: Leah Chen
description: Purpose: Provide a single-source PRD and operational playbook to guide the controlled removal of the legacy client transport (multiplexed longpoll/socket transport) and to require clients to adopt the Unified Inference transport by the end of Q2 2026. This document defines scope, product acceptance criteria, required engineering deliverables, observability requirements, migration paths for SDKs and third-party clients, customer communication, and rollback criteria. The goal is zero-severity customer outages while reducing maintenance surface area and simplifying platform routing policies.
scope: In-scope: API surface changes that affect client transport (endpoints, connection semantics, chunk framing, SSE vs streaming), SDK shims and adapters, migration CLI tooling, migration docs and example apps, telemetry gating and migration metrics. Out-of-scope: core model alias changes, billing model changes, or unrelated SDK language bindings that are not used by transport logic.
requirements: 1) Backward-compatible SDK adapters: Provide drop-in adapters in official SDKs (JS, Python, Go) that map legacy transport semantics to the Unified Inference transport with feature flags. 2) Server-side compatibility window: Support legacy transport behavior on the platform for a minimum of 90 days after GA of adapters. 3) Telemetry and blocking metrics: Implement migration telemetry to measure 1) % of customers still using legacy transport per org, 2) error rate delta post-migration, 3) latency p95 changes. 4) Migration CLI: Author a migration assistant CLI for large customers to validate connectivity and replay sample workloads. 5) Gradual enforcement plan: Implement a phased enforcement policy (warnings, disabled for new keys, opt-in shutoff, hard enforcement). 6) Docs & Playbooks: Detailed migration guide, compatibility matrix, FAQ, testing checklist, and runbooks for on-call. 7) Developer experience: Provide sample server and client code (websocket and fallback) and CI test harnesses to validate idempotency and reconnection behavior.
scope_changes: Change log for scope clarifications: 2026-03-04: Added explicit requirement for migration CLI after Sales requested tooling for 10 largest enterprise customers. 2026-03-07: Reduced server compatibility window from 180 to 90 days to align with capacity planning. 2026-03-09: Included explicit telemetry event names and retention policy per Security feedback.
acceptance_criteria: Official SDK adapters released for JS, Python, and Go with unit and integration tests; docs published and linked.
Platform maintains legacy transport endpoint for at least 90 days after adapters GA and returns deprecation header in legacy responses.
Migration telemetry dashboard available in Console showing per-org adoption and error/latency deltas; alerting configured for unusual error spikes.
Top 20 customers (by tokens/day) validated via migration CLI or manual runbook; any blockers have action plans assigned.
Automated compatibility tests show <0.1% increase in token failure rate across canary traffic during adapter shadowing.
Customer communications (email, console banner, docs) scheduled and approved; escalation playbook for enterprise support created.
Rollback criteria documented and verified in staging; smoke test runbooks executed successfully by SRE and Support teams.
migration_steps: Phase 0 - Prep (now -> 2026-03-31): Finalize adapters API; staff training; create migration CLI alpha; draft docs and example apps.
Phase 1 - Canary (2026-04-01 -> 2026-04-14): Release adapters as opt-in; start shadowing 5% of traffic with adapters in 'observe' mode; validate telemetry and error baselines.
Phase 2 - Broad opt-in (2026-04-15 -> 2026-05-15): Promote adapters to default in SDK patch releases; new API keys get warning headers; begin targeted outreach to top customers.
Phase 3 - Enforcement ramp (2026-05-16 -> 2026-06-15): Turn off legacy transport for new keys; issue hard deprecation notices to remaining orgs; offer one-on-one migration support windows.
Phase 4 - Full enforcement (target 2026-06-30): Disable legacy transport globally; post-mortem and retrospective; remove maintenance resources for legacy endpoints.
rollout_plan: Canary with traffic shadowing to detect regressions; maintain ability to toggle shadowing per-region and per-tenant.
Use per-org feature flags in console to opt specific customers into migration cohorts and record consent and outcomes.
Run weekly migration triage for top customers; assign owner for each blocking issue with SLA 5 business days for remediation.
Enable staged RBAC gating so Support can temporarily re-enable legacy transport for specific keys during live incidents to reduce customer impact.
monitoring_and_telemetry: New events: transport.deprecation.warning_sent, transport.migration.attempt, transport.adapter.error, transport.legacy.usage_report.
Dashboards: per-tenant adoption %, p50/p95 latency delta, token failure rate, reconnection frequency.
Alerts: >3x spike in adapter.error for a single tenant (P1), overall legacy usage week-over-week drop <4% after outreach window (P2).
Retention: migration telemetry retained 180 days for trend analysis; event names and retention updated per security review.
communication_plan: T-60 days: Announcement blog post + detailed migration guide published; console banners for Admins; email to all org owners.
T-30 days: Personalized outreach to top 200 customers with account plans; migration office hours scheduled weekly.
T-7 days: Final reminder + list of action items for customers; support hotline and ticket prioritization enabled.
Post-enforcement: Summary of outcomes, FAQs, and a feedback survey.
rollback_criteria: If canary shows >=1% absolute increase in token failure rate sustained for >1 hour across multiple regions -> pause enforcement and roll back adapters in canary cohort.
If any P0 outage attributable to transport migration (SLO breach) -> immediate pause of enforcement and create cross-functional incident war room.
If migration adapter causes >50ms median latency regression for top 10% of requests for >24 hours -> revert adapter change and investigate kernel/serialization path.
